elements.text: Heatline · capacity planning and job scheduling for residential heat-pump installers
Heatline is a fictional company. All company, product, customer, traction and financial figures
in this deck are illustrative. External figures are sourced and cited on the page where they appear.

pages.name: Why now: heat-pump sales and policy (+11%)

elements.text: The market turned. The exit became law.
heat pumps outsold gas boilers in
EPBD Article 17(15) ended incentives for new stand-alone fossil boilers in 2025; plans must reach full phase-out by 2040.
Sources: IEA Global Energy Review 2025 and 2026 · European Commission, Energy · retrieved 2026-09-10
more installers Europe needs — and at least half of
today's installers must be reskilled for heat pumps.
Schematic — shape of the gap, not a measured series.
In a survey of 345 installers, 30% named staffing the top barrier — 41% at firms with 6+ staff.
Lack of demand ranked higher overall (41%); staffing binds firms that already have work.
UK: about 3,000 heat-pump engineers today against at least 27,000 needed by 2028.
Sources: European Commission · EHPA · Nesta · retrieved 2026-09-10
Same schematic. The lever is jobs completed per engineer, not new hires.
Heatline does not train engineers and does not sell equipment. It plans the capacity a business has.
Product capability described on this page is illustrative.
